headline: Preparedness is readiness for what might come—having plans, supplies, and skills before you need them
universal_truth: Prepare when you can, not when you must; the time to get ready is before you need to be
fun_facts: Most experts recommend having at least 72 hours of supplies ready for emergencies
People with emergency plans respond faster and more effectively during crises
Preparation reduces both the objective danger and the subjective panic during emergencies
discussion_questions: How prepared are you for likely disruptions in your life?
What would you wish you had ready if something went wrong tomorrow?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Disasters rarely announce themselves. Power outages, accidents, job loss, health crises—they arrive suddenly. Preparedness means having plans, supplies, and skills before the moment arrives. The time to prepare is now, not when crisis hits.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We know we should prepare, but often don't. What's the real value of being ready before you have to be?

options.text: Preparation in calm times creates options in crisis—you can't buy insurance after the accident; readiness gives you resources when acquiring resources is impossible
options.response: Yes. During crisis, there's no time to prepare—only time to execute. What you prepared before determines what options you have during. Prepare while you can, not while you must.
Peace of mind matters, but the practical benefit is having options when you need them...

q1.title: Calm-Time Advantage
q1.script: Preparing during calm times is efficient—you can think clearly, gather resources, and plan thoroughly. Preparing during crisis is panicked, expensive, and often impossible.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Calm-Time Advantage"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Plans, Skills, Supplies
q2.script: Preparedness has three components: plans (what to do), skills (how to do it), and supplies (what to use). All three matter. Missing any one creates vulnerability.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Proportional Preparation
q3.script: Prepare proportionally to likelihood and consequence. Everyday disruptions are likely—be ready. Catastrophes are unlikely but severe—be somewhat ready. Don't over- or under-prepare.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Prepare when you can, not when you must. The time to get ready is before you need to be. Prepare now.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 314. Tomorrow, we'll explore weighing what could go wrong—risk assessment. Until then, consider your preparedness for likely disruptions.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Preparedness Check - What Are You Ready For?
growTrack.learning_objective: Assess and improve readiness for disruptions
growTrack.activity: What disruptions are reasonably likely in your life—power outage, job loss, illness, natural disaster? For each: Do you have a plan? Do you have skills? Do you have supplies? Identify gaps.
